## How to Change Ascendancy in PoE 2

Path of Exile 2 lets you switch to another Ascendancy of the same base class without making a new character. A Ranger can move from Pathfinder to Deadeye, a Witch from Infernalist to Lich. A Ranger can't take a Huntress Ascendancy — the base class never changes.
The switch itself takes three steps:
1. Complete an Ascension trial — Trial of the Sekhemas or Trial of Chaos.
2. Talk to Balbala or the Trialmaster and choose Change Ascendancy.
3. Pick the new Ascendancy at the device.
The hard part is the first step. That's the part our booster clears — self-play or piloted.
## What the PoE 2 Ascendancy Respec Includes
- The Ascension trial cleared on your character by an in-house booster
- Self-play from the booster's party or piloted on your account
- The new Ascendancy named by you, never chosen by the booster

## Respec or a New Character?
A new character means the campaign again, then every Ascension trial from the first tier. A respec keeps everything you've built and adds one trial — and we clear it for you.

A patch moves the meta, a build from the ladder looks stronger, or your Ascendancy stops scaling in late maps. The character is fine — only the Ascendancy is wrong. That's what this service fixes.

## How Ascension Trials Work in PoE 2

Path of Exile 2 gives 8 Ascendancy points through four tiers of Ascension trials, two points per tier. You earn them in the Trial of the Sekhemas or the Trial of Chaos, and every tier asks for a harder run than the one before.
A failed run means farming another entry item and starting over. That loop is what the boost removes: the booster finishes the run, you take the points.
